details:
AstroCare – Astronaut Health Companion

1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

AstroCare is a web-based health companion designed to help astronauts keep track of their health during space missions. Astronauts can enter important health information, such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep hours, and mood.

The website provides a daily health check-in, displays health trends, and gives simple educational feedback based on the information entered. It also includes information about different body systems, a mission checklist, and a spaceflight health guide. Users can save their records in the browser and export them as CSV files for later use.

2. What benefits does it have?

Living in space can be challenging for the human body and mind. AstroCare aims to make health tracking easier and more convenient for astronauts.

It helps them keep their health information organised, notice changes in their health over time, and pay attention to important areas such as sleep and mood. The health guides also help astronauts understand how space conditions can affect their bodies. Overall, the project encourages astronauts to take an active role in looking after their well-being.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The main goal of AstroCare is to support astronauts in staying healthy and well during long-duration space missions. We hope it will encourage regular health check-ins, improve awareness of physical and mental well-being, and help astronauts keep useful health records.

By making health information easier to track and understand, AstroCare could also support better communication with the crew's medical team when health concerns arise.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

We developed AstroCare using common web development technologies:

  • HTML5 – to build the structure of the website.
  • CSS3 – to create the design and layout.
  • JavaScript – to make the features interactive.
  • Browser Local Storage – to save health records and checklist progress on the user's device.
  • Canvas API – to display health trend charts.
  • CSV export – to allow users to download their health records.

The project runs in a web browser, so it does not require specialised hardware or medical sensors. Health information is entered manually, and the sample dashboard values are for demonstration purposes.

5. How is the project creative?

What makes AstroCare different is that it brings health tracking and space exploration together in one simple platform. Instead of focusing only on physical health, it also considers sleep, mood, and the mental challenges astronauts may experience in space.

We designed it with a modern, space-inspired interface and included interactive features such as health check-ins, charts, a mission checklist, and educational guides. Our aim was to make health monitoring feel simple, engaging, and relevant to the unique needs of astronauts.

6. What factors did the team consider?

While developing AstroCare, we considered the challenges astronauts may face during space missions, including:

  • Microgravity: How spending time in low gravity can affect the human body.
  • Radiation: The possible health risks of exposure to radiation in space.
  • Isolation: The effects of being away from family, friends, and Earth.
  • Physical health: The importance of monitoring basic health indicators.
  • Mental well-being: The role of sleep and mood in maintaining overall health.
  • Ease of use: Making the website simple and easy to navigate.
  • Accessibility: Keeping it lightweight and usable through a web browser.
  • Data management: Allowing users to save and export their records.
  • Medical safety: Making it clear that AstroCare is an educational prototype, not a certified medical device or a replacement for professional medical advice.

Our overall vision

With AstroCare, we wanted to create more than just a health-tracking website. We wanted to develop a simple and useful companion that reminds astronauts to look after themselves while exploring space. We believe that taking care of the people behind every space mission is just as important as the mission itself.
